name: Observation Post

placement_rationale.text: 4 km sits inside doctrine.md §2's close-reconnaissance depth (1-5 km, "activated within seconds of detection") and, on this map's own terrain, gravitates toward a real elevated treeline Pass 17 built — the same high-ground-plus-cover combination a human OP needs for line of sight without being skylined, not just a drone launch/observation position. A human OP and a drone team's launch point serve overlapping functions and plausibly share the same real ground.

representative_system: Manned observation post — composite, not a specific site

cost.display: Not a procurement item — a staffed position, not equipment

key_facts.label: Function
key_facts.value: Direct visual observation and call-for-fire cueing, backing up drone coverage

key_facts.label: Siting
key_facts.value: Elevated ground with tree cover — line of sight without being skylined

key_facts.label: Depth
key_facts.value: Doctrine's close-reconnaissance band, 1-5 km — activated within seconds of detection

short_role: A human-crewed lookout position on real high ground — line-of-sight coverage a drone's downward-looking camera doesn't fully replace.
characteristics: Sited on real elevated, tree-covered ground on this map, the same kind of terrain a drone team would also use — not an arbitrary point
Provides continuous human line-of-sight observation as a backup/cross-check to drone-fed coverage, which can be jammed, shot down, or simply not looking the right way
Feeds targeting and early-warning data into the same close-reconnaissance layer doctrine.md describes as activated within seconds of detection
Remains relevant even as drone ISR dominates, precisely because it doesn't depend on an uninterrupted radio link or battery endurance
employment_notes: Represents a generic manned OP rather than a specific coordinate, sited on real elevated/wooded ground this map already models rather than assumed open steppe. Works alongside, not instead of, the tactical reconnaissance drones already on this map — different failure modes, same close-in depth.
contrast_vs_traditional: A traditional OP was often the primary source of local battlefield awareness. It hasn't disappeared, but it's now one input among several — a drone can cover more ground and doesn't tire, but it can also be jammed, shot down or simply airborne elsewhere, which is why a human OP on real high ground still earns its place rather than being fully replaced.

connections.description: Cross-checks and supplements the same close-reconnaissance picture the tactical recon drone feeds.

notes: Written from doctrine.md and general knowledge; no per-asset citation yet.
